title: Mortal Kombat Is the Reason Games Have Age Ratings
hook: In December 1993 Mortal Kombat and Night Trap were hauled in front of the US Senate, and nine months later the ESRB was born. This week the Mortal Kombat II movie picked up a Game Awards nomination. Did your parents ever ban Mortal Kombat in your house?
script: Did you know Mortal Kombat is a big reason video games carry age ratings today? In September 1993, Acclaim brought the arcade hit home on a launch day it called Mortal Monday. Nintendo made the Super Nintendo version tone down the blood and the fatalities. Sega let Genesis players unlock the full gore with a code. The uproar reached Washington. In December 1993, Senators Joe Lieberman and Herb Kohl held a hearing on violent video games. Mortal Kombat and Night Trap were the main exhibits. Nintendo's Howard Lincoln and Sega's Bill White argued in front of the senators. White even held up a bazooka shaped light gun that Nintendo sold to make his point. Faced with the threat of government regulation, the rival companies formed a trade group. In September 1994, the Entertainment Software Rating Board was born. Every E, T and M on a game box traces back to that fight. Thirty three years later, Mortal Kombat is still swinging. This week the Mortal Kombat Two movie was nominated for Best Adaptation at The Game Awards. The nominees were announced on November 17, and the show airs on December 10. Did your parents ever ban Mortal Kombat in your house? Follow for more gaming history.
